## Functions

### `backoffMs`

Exponential backoff with jitter, capped at `maxDelayMs`. Honours a
numeric `Retry-After` header when the server sends one (capped at 30 s,
independent of `maxDelayMs`, exactly as the origin did). The jitter
matters for the per-leaf fan-outs: without it, six workers that fail
together retry together forever. Origin: `main.tsx:146-162`.

```ts
function backoffMs(attempt: number, baseDelayMs: number, retryAfter: string | null, maxDelayMs?: number): number;
```

### `buildUrl`

Joins `base` and `path` with exactly one `/` between them and appends
`params` as a query string. Array values are repeated under the same
key (`fq=a&fq=b`, as Solr expects); `undefined` values are skipped. If
the joined URL already carries a `?`, the new parameters are appended
with `&`. Pure string work, so a relative base such as `/brapi/v2` is
fine. Values are encoded by `URLSearchParams` (space becomes `+`).

```ts
function buildUrl(base: string, path: string, params?: Record<string, UrlParamValue>): string;
```

### `chunk`

Splits `items` into consecutive arrays of at most `size` elements
(the last may be shorter). `size` is floored and clamped to at least 1
so a bad value can never loop forever. An empty input yields no chunks.
Origin: the `i += CHUNK` slicing loop at `main.tsx:731-732`.

```ts
function chunk<T>(items: readonly T[], size: number): T[][];
```

### `defaultFetch`

Resolves the transport lazily at call time so a test that stubs
`globalThis.fetch` after module load still takes effect, and so the
global is invoked as a method (some browsers throw "Illegal invocation"
when `fetch` is called detached from `globalThis`).

```ts
function defaultFetch(input: string, init?: RequestInit): Promise<Response>;
```

### `fanOut`

Runs `worker(key, signal)` for every key with bounded concurrency
(default 6) and collects the outcomes. A rejecting worker is recorded
in `errors[key]` (its message) and counted in `progress.failed`; the
promise never rejects because of a worker. Each worker gets its own
`AbortSignal` derived from `opts.signal`. If `opts.signal` aborts
mid-run, in-flight workers see their signal abort and whatever they
then return or throw is recorded as usual, while keys not yet started
are recorded as `errors[key] = 'aborted'` without being run; the
promise still resolves once every key has settled, with
`progress.done === progress.total`. `onProgress` fires after each key
settles with a monotone `done`. Origin pattern: `main.tsx:512-651`.

```ts
function fanOut<V>(keys: readonly string[], worker: (key: string, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<V>, opts?: FanOutOptions): Promise<FanOutResult<V>>;
```

### `fanOutChunks`

Like {@link fanOut} but one worker call answers for a whole chunk of
keys: `keys` are split with {@link chunk} into groups of `size`, the
worker receives each group and returns a record of per-key values,
and every returned record is merged into `results` (later chunks win
on duplicate keys). A rejecting worker records its message under
every key of that chunk; chunks never started because `opts.signal`
aborted record `'aborted'` for their keys. `progress` and `onProgress`
count individual keys, not chunks, so a 400-gene tree fetched 200 at a
time reports `done` as 0, 200, 400. Origin pattern: `main.tsx:727-753`.

```ts
function fanOutChunks<V>(keys: readonly string[], size: number, worker: (keys: string[], signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<Record<string, V>>, opts?: FanOutOptions): Promise<FanOutResult<V>>;
```

### `fetchWithRetry`

`fetch` with bounded retries for the failure modes Ensembl REST shows
under load: 429, 5xx, and dropped connections. Returns the final
response even when it is still a failure, so callers keep their
existing `res.ok` handling; only a network-level error (the transport
rejecting on every attempt) throws. Non-retryable statuses such as 404
are returned immediately without a retry. Origin: `main.tsx:164-191`.

```ts
function fetchWithRetry(url: string, init?: RequestInit, opts?: RetryOptions): Promise<Response>;
```

### `getJson`

GET `url` with `Accept: application/json` and parse the body. Throws
{@link HttpError} (with the body text when readable) on any non-2xx
status; the `signal` is passed straight to the transport so callers can
cancel. Extra `headers` are merged after `Accept`, so they may override
it.

```ts
function getJson<T = unknown>(url: string, opts?: {
    fetch?: FetchLike;
    signal?: AbortSignal;
    headers?: Record<string, string>;
}): Promise<T>;
```

### `mergeRecords`

Shallow-merges any number of records into a new object, skipping
`undefined` parts; later parts win on duplicate keys. Convenience for
combining the per-chunk records a batched endpoint returns
(`main.tsx:746`).

```ts
function mergeRecords<V>(...parts: ReadonlyArray<Record<string, V> | undefined>): Record<string, V>;
```

### `splitUrl`

Inverse of {@link buildUrl}: splits a URL at its first `?` into the
path (everything before it, which may be a relative or absolute URL)
and a `URLSearchParams` of the query string. A URL without `?` yields
empty params. Fragments are not treated specially.

```ts
function splitUrl(url: string): {
    path: string;
    params: URLSearchParams;
};
```

### `withRetry`

Wraps a transport so every call goes through {@link fetchWithRetry}
with the given options. This is what the data-source loader hands to
sources as their `fetch`, so individual sources never think about
retries.

```ts
function withRetry(fetch: FetchLike, opts?: Omit<RetryOptions, 'fetch'>): FetchLike;
```

## Classes

### `HttpError`

Thrown by {@link getJson} when the response is not `ok`. Carries the
status, the requested URL and, when it could be read, the response body
text so callers can surface the server's own message (Solr and BrAPI
both put useful detail there).

```ts
class HttpError extends Error {
    readonly status: number;
    readonly url: string;
    readonly bodyText?: string;
    constructor(status: number, url: string, bodyText?: string);
}
```

## Constants

### `RETRYABLE_STATUS`

Transient statuses worth another attempt. Ensembl sheds load with 5xx
and rate-limits with 429; every other 4xx is a real client error
(deprecated accession, unknown id) that retrying cannot fix. 520/522/524
are Cloudflare's origin-unreachable codes, seen on mirrors fronted by it.
Origin: `main.tsx:141`.

```ts
const RETRYABLE_STATUS: ReadonlySet<number>;
```

## Interfaces

### `FanOutOptions`

Options accepted by {@link fanOut} and {@link fanOutChunks}.

```ts
interface FanOutOptions {
    /** Maximum keys in flight at once (default 6; values below 1 are treated as 1). */
    concurrency?: number;
    /**
     * Aborting this signal aborts every in-flight worker's own signal and
     * marks every key not yet started as failed with the message
     * `'aborted'`. The returned promise still resolves.
     */
    signal?: AbortSignal;
    /** Called after each key settles; `done` only ever increases. */
    onProgress?: (p: FanOutProgress) => void;
}
```

### `FanOutProgress`

Running tally reported to `onProgress` and returned in the result.

```ts
interface FanOutProgress {
    /** Keys settled so far (successes + failures). Monotone. */
    done: number;
    /** Total number of keys. Constant for the run. */
    total: number;
    /** Keys that failed so far. Monotone, `<= done`. */
    failed: number;
}
```

### `FanOutResult`

What {@link fanOut} and {@link fanOutChunks} resolve to.

```ts
interface FanOutResult<V> {
    /** Successful values keyed by input key. */
    results: Record<string, V>;
    /** Failure messages keyed by input key (`'aborted'` for keys never started). */
    errors: Record<string, string>;
    /** Final tally; `done === total` on resolution. */
    progress: FanOutProgress;
    /** Message of the most recent failure, or `null` when nothing failed. */
    lastError: string | null;
}
```

### `RetryOptions`

Options accepted by {@link fetchWithRetry} and {@link withRetry}.

```ts
interface RetryOptions {
    /** Total attempts including the first (default 4). */
    attempts?: number;
    /** Base of the exponential backoff in milliseconds (default 500). */
    baseDelayMs?: number;
    /** Cap on the exponential backoff in milliseconds (default 8000). */
    maxDelayMs?: number;
    /** Statuses that trigger a retry (default {@link RETRYABLE_STATUS}). */
    retryable?: ReadonlySet<number>;
    /** Transport to use (default `globalThis.fetch`). */
    fetch?: FetchLike;
}
```

## Type aliases

### `FetchLike`

The structural subset of WHATWG `fetch` that this library needs: a
string URL plus an optional `RequestInit`, resolving to a `Response`.
Every network-facing helper in `tbrowse-core` takes one of these so
callers can wrap, record, stub or rate-limit it.

```ts
type FetchLike = (input: string, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>;
```

### `UrlParamValue`

Query-parameter value accepted by {@link buildUrl}.

```ts
type UrlParamValue = string | number | readonly (string | number)[] | undefined;
```
